requirements.rationale: An agent that cannot see what its query returns saves wrong numbers with confidence.
requirements.statement: Any agent can run a read-only query over the current project's data and receive its columns and rows, so it can check a query's result before it saves a dashboard.

requirements.rationale: One database holds every project on the Hub; the roadmap is heading towards other users' projects.
requirements.statement: A query never returns a row belonging to another project, whatever the query text says, including queries that omit a project filter, join tables, or read the list of projects.

A query cannot read credentials (API keys, operator credentials, run tokens, the trace exporter's headers) or this machine's paths (the project directory, run workspaces, workspace fingerprints); a query naming them is refused with a message saying what is not queryable.
A query cannot change any data: an insert, update, delete, schema change or attach is refused and the data is unchanged.

requirements.rationale: The operator wants to count leaks and occurrences of things in the conversations.
requirements.statement: Free-text data is queryable — agent output, the traces' tool arguments and results, model messages and command lines, and message, queue and checkpoint text — and a query can match a regular expression against any text column.
A query that runs longer than 10 seconds is stopped and answers an error saying so, and a result over 10,000 rows is cut to 10,000 and says it was cut.

requirements.rationale: On 2026-11-13 ordinary reads already take 1.5-3 s during builds on a 920 MB database; the heaviest read anyone will ask for must not add to that.
requirements.statement: While dashboard queries run — including a regular-expression search over every trace span and a query stopped at the time limit — the Hub's event loop never stalls for more than 100 ms, and a GET /agents made meanwhile answers within 500 ms on a copy of the operator's database.

requirements.rationale: A hand-written description goes stale on the first migration.
requirements.statement: The Hub provides agents a reference of everything a query can reach — each table and column, its type and a short meaning — generated from the running version, and nothing in it is refused when queried.

Every project's vault holds a note on what the data means and its traps, present before any dashboard tool is first called — including in projects registered before this ships — and never overwritten once agents have added to it; the agent tools point agents to it, and it is seeded with the known traps (a send-back rejects every piece of evidence from that commit; cost per spec counts its tasks' building and reviewing runs).

requirements.rationale: A Hub upgrade can break a saved query anyway, so a failing panel has to be handled on the screen regardless.
requirements.statement: An agent can save a dashboard to the current project with a name, a description of the question it answers, and panels, each with a title, a query and a chart kind; the dashboard records which agent made it and when, and survives a Hub restart. Saving checks chart kinds and the never-queryable boundary but does not run the queries, so a panel whose query fails can be saved.
A panel's chart kind is one of a fixed set — single number, table, bar, stacked bar and line — and every kind is drawn in the app's colours and type, readable in both light and dark themes.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-13: the screen is local, and a masked leak cannot be found.
requirements.statement: A table panel shows every value its query returns in full, free text included; no value is masked or redacted.

The project has a Dashboards screen, reachable from the app's navigation, listing its dashboards with name, author and date; opening one runs all its queries and draws them, a Refresh button runs them again, and the dashboard shows when its data was last fetched. The operator can delete a dashboard there.

A panel whose query fails shows the error on that panel, and a panel whose result cannot be drawn as its chart kind (for example a line with no numeric column) shows a warning saying why; the other panels still draw.
Deleting a project removes its dashboards.

requirements.rationale: A second near-duplicate dashboard per request is the failure the roadmap slice exists to remove.
requirements.statement: Asked to change an existing dashboard, an agent edits that saved dashboard: afterwards the project holds the same number of dashboards, the dashboard keeps its identity, and the Dashboards screen shows the change on the dashboard the operator already had.

requirements.rationale: Guessing between two dashboards edits the wrong one without anyone noticing.
requirements.statement: The agent edits the dashboard the operator means: the one named in the request, or the one the operator's Ask to change named; when the name matches no dashboard, or several, or no dashboard is named, the agent says so and asks which, and changes nothing and creates nothing.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-14: what the agent is told stays visible, rather than a hidden context the operator cannot see.
requirements.statement: An open dashboard on the Dashboards screen offers Ask to change: the operator picks an agent, that agent's conversation opens, and its composer holds an editable line naming the dashboard's name and identifier, sent only when the operator sends it.

requirements.rationale: The operator trusts a dashboard they have looked at; an edit that quietly rewrites other panels breaks that.
requirements.statement: An edit changes only what was asked: every panel, query, title, chart kind, panel id, the order of panels, the name and description that the request did not mention are unchanged after the edit.

requirements.rationale: A half-applied edit leaves a dashboard nobody asked for.
requirements.statement: The Hub applies an edit as a list of operations (add a panel, remove a panel, change a panel's title, query or chart kind, move a panel, rename or re-describe the dashboard); if any operation is refused, including a chart kind outside the fixed set, a panel that does not exist, or a name another dashboard of the project holds, no operation is applied and the refusal says which and why.

requirements.rationale: An agent works from what it read at the start of a long turn; the operator or another agent may have edited since.
requirements.statement: An edit or a whole replace made against a version of the dashboard that is no longer the current one is refused with a message saying the dashboard changed and the current dashboard, and nothing is overwritten.

requirements.rationale: Asking for changes is only safe if a wrong one costs one click.
requirements.statement: After an edit or a whole replace the Hub keeps the version it replaced, and the operator can restore it in one step from the Dashboards screen (and an agent can when asked); restoring is itself an edit, so it can be undone the same way; a dashboard with no earlier version offers nothing to restore.

requirements.rationale: Slice first-dashboard surfaces a broken panel but cannot mend it; this is the other half.
requirements.statement: An agent can run a saved dashboard and receive, for each panel, its result or its error and drawing warning, exactly as the screen shows them; asked to fix a broken panel, it can correct that panel's query from its error, check the new result, and change only that panel, after which the panel draws.

requirements.rationale: The edit path must not become a way round the query boundary.
requirements.statement: An edit's queries are held to the same limits as slice first-dashboard's saves (current project only, read-only, never-queryable data refused), and an agent cannot edit, undo, run or read the kept version of a dashboard belonging to another project.
Deleting a dashboard, or the project it belongs to, removes its kept earlier version.
The Dashboards screen shows who last edited the dashboard and when, beside the author and date.

requirements.rationale: Tests, drives and screen readers read the page; a count-up must not make them read a wrong figure.
requirements.statement: On opening a dashboard, its panels appear one after another, bars grow from their start, lines trace from left to right, points appear after their line, and a number counts up to its value, all within 1.5 seconds; throughout, the number's element holds its real value, and no figure read from the page is ever a mid-animation value.

When an open dashboard's queries run again (Refresh, or an agent saving that dashboard), its charts dim while the queries run and then bars, lines and points move to their new values rather than the panel being redrawn from empty.

requirements.rationale: Shows the operator what an agent's change did without comparing before and after by eye.
requirements.statement: When the open dashboard gains a panel, that panel is marked once as new as it appears; when it loses one, that panel fades out where it was before it is gone; on first opening a dashboard no panel is marked new.

Hovering a bar segment or a line point shows a tooltip in the app's own style naming the point's label, its series and its value, and dims the other marks of that chart; leaving the mark removes both.

While a dashboard's queries first run, placeholders shaped like its panels (up to four) stand where the panels will be; the first carries the app's loading thread with the words 'Running its queries', the others are still, and nothing on the screen shimmers. The placeholders are gone once the run arrives, and are not shown when the run fails.
When the system asks for reduced motion, nothing on the Dashboards screen animates: panels, charts and numbers appear at their final state at once, and the tooltip and dimming still work.

The save tool's guidance tells an agent which kind suits which question (one figure: number; a ranking or comparison: bar; parts of a whole across labels: stacked bar; change over time: line; detail rows: table), and how to shape a query to read well: order rows as they should be drawn, keep bar charts to about 15 labels by taking the top ones, put time in order for a line, and alias columns to the readable names the legend and tooltip will show.

requirements.rationale: An example that does not draw teaches the wrong thing; each is checked by running it.
requirements.statement: The data note every project's vault is seeded with carries one worked example per chart kind, each a query over that project's own data and its kind, and each example draws with no warning on a project that has tasks and runs.

Asked in plain words for a dashboard needing each of the five kinds, an agent on the project's cheapest model produces a dashboard whose every panel draws with no error and no drawing warning on first opening.
